the tāʾ is nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) and the mīm is the sign of the masculine plural. ﴿بِهِ﴾ attached to فتنتم; the clause is the maqūl al-qawl. ﴿وَإِنَّ رَبَّكُمُ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and inna and its noun; the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿الرَّحْمنُ﴾ khabar; the clause is conjoined. ﴿فَاتَّبِعُونِي﴾ the fāʾ is the faṣīḥa fāʾ (al-fāʾ al-faṣīḥa); اتبعوني is an imperative verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the deletion of the nūn; the nūn is for protection (wiqāya) and the yāʾ is mafʿūl bihi. ﴿وَأَطِيعُوا﴾ the clause is conjoined. ﴿أَمْرِي﴾ mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb) by the fatḥa implied (muqaddara) on the letter before the yāʾ of the first person, its appearance being prevented by the place being occupied by the vowel suited [to the yāʾ]; the clause is conjoined.

daas-irab:91-94.t:
﴿قالُوا﴾ the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya). ﴿لَنْ﴾ making [the verb] accusative. ﴿نَبْرَحَ﴾ an incomplete (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by lan; its noun is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "نحن". ﴿عَلَيْهِ﴾ [a preposition and its genitive noun] attached to (mutaʿalliq) عاكفين. ﴿عاكِفِينَ﴾ the khabar (predicate) of نبرح; the clause is the maqūl al-qawl (object of the saying). ﴿حَتَّى﴾ a particle of limit and a preposition. ﴿يَرْجِعَ﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied (muḍmara) an after ḥattā. ﴿إِلَيْنا﴾ attached to يرجع. ﴿مُوسى﴾ fāʿil (agent). يرجع and the implied an before it are interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of genitive by ḥattā, and [the two are] attached to عاكفين. ﴿قالَ﴾ the clause is resumptive. ﴿يا هارُونُ﴾ yā is a vocative particle, and the one addressed (munādā); the clause is in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of قال. ﴿ما﴾ an interrogative noun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿مَنَعَكَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent; the kāf is mafʿūl bihi; the clause is the khabar of mā. ﴿إِذْ﴾ an adverb attached to منعك. ﴿رَأَيْتَهُمْ﴾ a past verb, fāʿil and mafʿūl bihi; the clause is in the position of genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿ضَلُّوا﴾ a past verb and fāʿil; the clause is in the position of accusative as the second mafʿūl bihi of رأيتهم, on the view that it is [a verb] of the heart (qalbiyya). ﴿أن﴾ a maṣdar-forming particle that makes the verb accusative. ﴿لا﴾ redundant (zāʾida). ﴿تَتَّبِعَنِ﴾ an accusative imperfect verb; the nūn is for protection (wiqāya), the fāʿil is latent, and the deleted yāʾ is mafʿūl bihi; it was also read with the yāʾ retained. An and what follows it are interpreted as a maṣdar in the position of genitive by an implied preposition, min, and [the two are] attached to the verb. ﴿أَفَعَصَيْتَ﴾ the hamza is for rebuking interrogation (al-istifhām al-inkārī), the fāʾ is a conjunction, and عصيت is a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿أَمْرِي﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the yāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is conjoined to an omitted, implied clause.
[Translator's note: from this point the source text is damaged — the brackets around the Quranic cue words are corrupted and several words are truncated. The cue words below are restored from the verse (20:94); the analyses are translated as they stand.]
﴿قالَ﴾ the clause is resumptive. ﴿يا﴾ a vocative particle. ﴿بْنَ أُمَّ﴾ two nouns compounded together, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of accusative as the one addressed. ﴿لا﴾ prohibitive. ﴿تَأْخُذْ﴾ a jussive (majzūm) imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿بِلِحْيَتِي﴾ attached to تأخذ. ﴿وَلا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction and lā is prohibitive, entering upon an omitted verb. ﴿بِرَأْسِي﴾ attached to تأخذ, and it is conjoined; the vocative clause and what follows it are the maqūl al-qawl. ﴿إِنِّي﴾ inna and its noun; the clause is causal (taʿlīliyya). ﴿خَشِيتُ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of inna. ﴿أَنْ﴾ making [the verb] accusative. ﴿تَقُولَ﴾ an accusative imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is a khabar. ﴿فَرَّقْتَ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿بَيْنَ﴾ an adverb of place. ﴿بَنِي﴾ muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr) by the yāʾ. ﴿إِسْرائِيلَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi, genitive by the fatḥa because it is a diptote; the clause is the maqūl al-qawl. ﴿وَلَمْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction and lam makes [the verb] jussive. ﴿تَرْقُبْ﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive by it; its fāʿil is latent. ﴿قَوْلِي﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the yāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa).

daas-irab:95-96.t: ﴿قالَ﴾ the clause is resumptive. ﴿فَما﴾ the fāʾ is redundant (zāʾida); mā is an interrogative noun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿خَطْبُكَ﴾ khabar (predicate); the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿يا سامِرِيُّ﴾ yā is a vocative particle, and سامري is the one addressed (munādā), indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma in the position of accusative; the nominal clause and the vocative are in the position of accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of the saying). ﴿قالَ﴾ the clause is resumptive. ﴿بَصُرْتُ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿بِما﴾ the preposition and the relative mā are attached to (mutaʿalliq) بصرت; the clause is the maqūl al-qawl. ﴿لَمْ﴾ making [the verb] jussive. ﴿يَبْصُرُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the deletion of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause), with no position. ﴿بِهِ﴾ attached to يبصروا. ﴿فَقَبَضْتُ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and قبضت is a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿قَبْضَةً﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). ﴿مِنْ أَثَرِ﴾ attached to قبضت. ﴿الرَّسُولِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. The trace of the messenger is the trace of the hoof of the horse of our master Gabriel, peace be upon him. The clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa). ﴿فَنَبَذْتُها﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a past verb, its fāʿil and its object; the clause is conjoined. ﴿وَكَذلِكَ﴾ the wāw is resumptive, and the preposition and the genitive demonstrative are attached to an omitted adjective (ṣifa) of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq, its implied form being "my soul enticed me with an enticement like that enticement … etc.". ﴿سَوَّلَتْ﴾ a past verb; the tāʾ is for the feminine. ﴿لِي﴾ attached to سولت. ﴿نَفْسِي﴾ fāʿil; the yāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is resumptive.

daas-irab:97-97.t: ﴿قالَ﴾ the clause is resumptive. ﴿فَاذْهَبْ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and the imperative verb's fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa). ﴿فَإِنَّ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction and inna is a particle resembling the verb. ﴿لَكَ﴾ [a preposition and its genitive noun] attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate). ﴿فِي الْحَياةِ﴾ attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿أَنْ﴾ making [the verb] accusative. ﴿تَقُولَ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; the interpreted maṣdar is in the position of accusative as the noun of inna. ﴿لا﴾ the lā of generic negation. ﴿مِساسَ﴾ the noun of lā; the khabar is omitted; the clause is in the position of accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of the saying). It is said that al-Sāmirī was afflicted with an illness resembling gout, so that anything that touched him hurt him, and that was a punishment for him in this world. ﴿وَإِنَّ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction and inna is a particle resembling the verb. ﴿لَكَ﴾ attached to the fronted khabar. ﴿مَوْعِداً﴾ its postponed noun. ﴿لَنْ﴾ making [the verb] accusative. ﴿تُخْلَفَهُ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb); the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is in the position of accusative as an adjective (ṣifa) of موعدا. ﴿وَانْظُرْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and انظر is an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿إِلى إِلهِكَ﴾ attached to انظر. ﴿الَّذِي﴾ a relative in the position of genitive as an adjective; the clause is conjoined. ﴿ظَلْتَ﴾ an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb; its original form is ظللت, the lām being deleted for lightening; the tāʾ is its noun. ﴿عَلَيْهِ﴾ attached to عاكفا. ﴿عاكِفاً﴾ khabar; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative, with no position. ﴿لَنُحَرِّقَنَّهُ﴾ the lām prepares for the oath (muwaṭṭiʾa lil-qasam), and نحرقنه is an imperfect verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because it is joined to the heavy nūn of emphasis; its fāʿil is latent and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi; the clause has no grammatical position because it is the answer of the oath. ﴿ثُمَّ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿لَنَنْسِفَنَّهُ﴾ the clause is conjoined. ﴿فِي الْيَمِّ﴾ attached to the verb before them. ﴿نَسْفاً﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object).

daas-irab:98-100.t: ﴿إِنَّما﴾ the restraining [mā] and the restrained [inna] (kāffa wa-makfūfa). ﴿إِلهُكُمُ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject); the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿اللَّهُ﴾ the Name of Majesty, khabar (predicate); the clause is resumptive. ﴿الَّذِي﴾ a relative in the position of nominative as an adjective (ṣifa). ﴿لا﴾ the lā of generic negation. ﴿إِلهَ﴾ its noun; the khabar is omitted, its implied form being "موجود". ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿هُوَ﴾ badal (substitute) of the pronoun implied in the khabar; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause), with no position. ﴿وَسِعَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿كُلَّ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿شَيْءٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿عِلْماً﴾ tamyīz (specification); the clause is resumptive. ﴿كَذلِكَ﴾ the preposition and the demonstrative are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an adjective of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), its implied form being "We relate to you a relating like that which We have related to you". ﴿نَقُصُّ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya). ﴿عَلَيْكَ﴾ attached to نقص. ﴿مِنْ أَنْباءِ﴾ attached to the verb نقص. ﴿ما﴾ a relative, muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿قَدْ سَبَقَ﴾ the clause is the ṣila, with no position. ﴿وَقَدْ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); qad is a particle of realisation (taḥqīq). ﴿آتَيْناكَ﴾ a past verb, fāʿil and first mafʿūl bihi; the clause is circumstantial. ﴿مِنْ لَدُنَّا﴾ attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of ذكرا. ﴿ذِكْراً﴾ second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿مَنْ﴾ a jussive conditional noun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ. ﴿أَعْرَضَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent, in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ). ﴿عَنْهُ﴾ attached to أعرض; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa). ﴿فَإِنَّهُ﴾ the fāʾ is linking, and inna and its noun; the clause ﴿يَحْمِلُ﴾ is its khabar, and the clause فإنه is in the position of jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). ﴿يَوْمَ﴾ an adverb of time. ﴿الْقِيامَةِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وِزْراً﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the two clauses of the condition are the khabar of man.

daas-irab:101-104.t: ﴿خالِدِينَ﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative (manṣūb) by the yāʾ. ﴿فِيهِ﴾ [a preposition and its genitive noun] attached to (mutaʿalliq) خالدين. ﴿وَساءَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction; ساء is a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), and ساء is one of the verbs of blame. ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ attached to ساء. ﴿يَوْمَ﴾ an adverb of time, attached to حملا. ﴿الْقِيامَةِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿حِمْلًا﴾ tamyīz (specification); the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa). ﴿يَوْمَ﴾ badal (substitute) of يوم القيامة. ﴿يُنْفَخُ﴾ a passive imperfect verb whose nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent; the clause is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿فِي الصُّورِ﴾ attached to ينفخ. ﴿وَنَحْشُرُ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and the imperfect verb's fāʿil is latent, its implied form being "نحن". ﴿الْمُجْرِمِينَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is conjoined. ﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ﴾ an adverb annexed to an adverb, attached to نحشر. ﴿زُرْقاً﴾ ḥāl, i.e. from the effect of the punishment. ﴿يَتَخافَتُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is a ḥāl. ﴿بَيْنَهُمْ﴾ an adverb attached to the verb before it. ﴿إِنْ﴾ negative. ﴿لَبِثْتُمْ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿عَشْراً﴾ an adverb of time, attached to لبثتم; the clause is interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi of an omitted saying, its implied form being "قائلين" (saying). ﴿نَحْنُ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿أَعْلَمُ﴾ khabar (predicate). ﴿بِما﴾ the preposition and the relative noun are attached to أعلم; the clause is resumptive. ﴿يَقُولُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause), with no position. ﴿إِذْ﴾ an adverb attached to أعلم. ﴿يَقُولُ﴾ the clause is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿أَمْثَلُهُمْ﴾ fāʿil; the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿طَرِيقَةً﴾ tamyīz. ﴿إِنْ﴾ negative. ﴿لَبِثْتُمْ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction. ﴿يَوْماً﴾ an adverb attached to لبثتم.

daas-irab:105-108.t: ﴿وَيَسْئَلُونَكَ﴾ the wāw is resumptive; يسألون is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil (agent) and the kāf is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is resumptive. ﴿عَنِ الْجِبالِ﴾ [a preposition and its genitive noun] attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿فَقُلْ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and قل is an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir); the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa). ﴿يَنْسِفُها﴾ a nominative imperfect verb; the hāʾ is in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi. ﴿رَبِّي﴾ a postponed fāʿil; the yāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿نَسْفاً﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); the clause is in the position of accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of the saying). ﴿فَيَذَرُها﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and the imperfect verb's fāʿil is latent; the hāʾ is in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi; the clause is conjoined. ﴿قاعاً﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿صَفْصَفاً﴾ a second ḥāl. ﴿لا﴾ negative. ﴿تَرى﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative by the implied (muqaddara) ḍamma; its fāʿil is latent. ﴿فِيها﴾ attached to ترى. ﴿عِوَجاً﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿وَلا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction. ﴿لا﴾ negative. ﴿أَمْتاً﴾ conjoined to عوجا. ﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ﴾ يوم is an adverb attached to يتبعون, and idh is an adverb, muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿يَتَّبِعُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil. ﴿الدَّاعِيَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb) by the fatḥa; the clause is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿لا﴾ the lā of generic negation. ﴿عِوَجَ﴾ the noun of lā. ﴿لَهُ﴾ attached to the omitted khabar (predicate); the clause is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl of الداعي. ﴿وَخَشَعَتِ﴾ the wāw is resumptive, and a past verb; the tāʾ is for the feminine. ﴿الْأَصْواتُ﴾ fāʿil. ﴿لِلرَّحْمنِ﴾ attached to خشعت; the clause is resumptive. ﴿فَلا﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction. ﴿لا﴾ negative. ﴿تَسْمَعُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿هَمْساً﴾ mafʿūl bihi of تسمع; the clause is conjoined.

daas-irab:109-111.t: ﴿يوم﴾ an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) تنفع. ﴿إذ﴾ an adverb, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿لا﴾ negative. ﴿تَنْفَعُ الشَّفاعَةُ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿مَنْ﴾ a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿أَذِنَ﴾ a past verb. ﴿لَهُ﴾ [a preposition and its genitive noun] attached to the verb. ﴿الرَّحْمنُ﴾ fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause), with no position. ﴿وَرَضِيَ﴾ the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa). ﴿لَهُ﴾ attached to رضي. ﴿قَوْلًا﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿يَعْلَمُ﴾ a nominative (marfūʿ) imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir). ﴿ما﴾ a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi. ﴿بَيْنَ﴾ an adverb of place, attached to an omitted ṣila. ﴿أَيْدِيهِمْ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَما خَلْفَهُمْ﴾ the clause is conjoined. ﴿وَلا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction and lā is negative. ﴿يُحِيطُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is conjoined. ﴿بِهِ﴾ attached to يحيطون. ﴿عِلْماً﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿وَعَنَتِ﴾ the wāw is resumptive, and عنت is a past verb; the tāʾ is for the feminine. ﴿الْوُجُوهُ﴾ fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. ﴿لِلْحَيِّ﴾ attached to عنت. ﴿الْقَيُّومِ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa). ﴿وَقَدْ خابَ﴾ the clause is circumstantial (ḥāliyya). ﴿مَنْ﴾ a relative noun, fāʿil. ﴿حَمَلَ﴾ the clause is the ṣila, with no position. ﴿ظُلْماً﴾ mafʿūl bihi.

daas-irab:112-113.t:
﴿وَمَنْ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and man is a jussive conditional noun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause is resumptive. ﴿يَعْمَلْ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); يعمل is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ). ﴿مِنَ الصَّالِحاتِ﴾ [a preposition and its genitive noun] attached to (mutaʿalliq) يعمل. ﴿وَهُوَ مُؤْمِنٌ﴾ the wāw is the wāw of circumstance (ḥāl), and mubtadaʾ and khabar (predicate); the clause is circumstantial (ḥāliyya). ﴿فَلا﴾ the fāʾ links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); lā is negative. ﴿يَخافُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿ظُلْماً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿وَلا هَضْماً﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and هضما is conjoined to ظلما; the clause is in the position of jussive as the apodosis, and the two clauses of the condition are the khabar of the mubtadaʾ man. ﴿وَكَذلِكَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, the kāf is a preposition, and ذا is a demonstrative in the position of genitive — the lām is for distance and the kāf is for address — [the two being] attached to an omitted adjective (ṣifa) of a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), its implied form being "We sent it down a sending down being like … etc.".
﴿أَنْزَلْناهُ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its object. ﴿قُرْآناً﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿عَرَبِيًّا﴾ an adjective; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa). ﴿وَصَرَّفْنا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction; صرفنا is a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿فِيهِ﴾ attached to صرفنا. ﴿مِنَ الْوَعِيدِ﴾ the preposition and its genitive noun are an adjective of an omitted mafʿūl bihi, its implied form being "We varied a threat from among the threats"; the clause ﴿صَرَّفْنا﴾ is conjoined. ﴿لَعَلَّهُمْ﴾ laʿalla and its noun. ﴿يَتَّقُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is the khabar. ﴿أَوْ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿يُحْدِثُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent, referring back to the Qur'an. ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ attached to يحدث. ﴿ذِكْراً﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the clause is conjoined.

daas-irab:114-115.t: ﴿فَتَعالَى﴾ the fāʾ is resumptive; تعالى is a past verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the implied (muqaddara) fatḥa. ﴿اللَّهُ﴾ the Name of Majesty, fāʿil (agent). ﴿الْمَلِكُ الْحَقُّ﴾ two nominative adjectives (ṣifa); the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَلا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction and lā is prohibitive. ﴿تَعْجَلْ﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive lā; its fāʿil is latent (mustatir). ﴿بِالْقُرْآنِ﴾ [a preposition and its genitive noun] attached to (mutaʿalliq) تعجل. ﴿مِنْ قَبْلِ﴾ attached to تعجل. ﴿أَنْ﴾ making [the verb] accusative. ﴿يُقْضى﴾ a passive imperfect verb. ﴿إِلَيْكَ﴾ attached to يقضى. ﴿وَحْيُهُ﴾ nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَقُلْ﴾ the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa). ﴿رَبِّ﴾ the one addressed (munādā) with an omitted vocative particle; it is accusative as a vocative and annexed to the omitted yāʾ of the first person. ﴿زِدْنِي﴾ a verb of supplication; the nūn is for protection (wiqāya) and the yāʾ is in the position of accusative as the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿عِلْماً﴾ second mafʿūl bihi; the vocative clause and the one after it are the maqūl al-qawl (object of the saying). ﴿وَلَقَدْ﴾ the wāw is resumptive, the lām occurs in the answer of an omitted oath, and qad is a particle of realisation (taḥqīq). ﴿عَهِدْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿إِلى آدَمَ﴾ attached to عهدنا. ﴿مِنْ﴾ a preposition; qabl is an adverb indeclinable on the ḍamma in the position of genitive; [the two are] attached to عهدنا or to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); the clause is resumptive. ﴿فَنَسِيَ﴾ the clause is conjoined by the fāʾ. ﴿وَلَمْ نَجِدْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction and lam is a jussive particle; نجد is a jussive imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿لَهُ﴾ attached to نجد. ﴿عَزْماً﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the clause is conjoined.

daas-irab:116-117.t: ﴿وَإِذْ﴾ the wāw is resumptive; idh is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) [an implied] اذكر. ﴿قُلْنا﴾ the clause is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿لِلْمَلائِكَةِ﴾ [a preposition and its genitive noun] attached to قلنا. ﴿اسْجُدُوا﴾ an imperative verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the deletion of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil (agent). ﴿لِآدَمَ﴾ the lām is a preposition; آدم is genitive (majrūr) by the fatḥa in place of the kasra because it is a diptote; the clause is the maqūl al-qawl (object of the saying). ﴿فَسَجَدُوا﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa). ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of exception. ﴿إِبْلِيسَ﴾ excepted by illā, accusative (manṣūb) by the fatḥa. ﴿أَبى﴾ a past verb indeclinable on the implied (muqaddara) fatḥa; its fāʿil is latent (mustatir); the clause is in the position of accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿فَقُلْنا﴾ the fāʾ is resumptive, and قلنا is a past verb and fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. ﴿يا آدَمُ﴾ yā is a vocative particle; آدم is the one addressed (munādā), a singular proper noun, indeclinable on the ḍamma, in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of أدعو. ﴿إِنَّ﴾ a particle resembling the verb. ﴿هذا﴾ the hāʾ is for drawing attention (tanbīh), and ذا is a demonstrative in the position of accusative as the noun of inna. ﴿عَدُوٌّ﴾ khabar (predicate). ﴿لَكَ﴾ attached to عدو. ﴿وَلِزَوْجِكَ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it; the kāf is in the position of genitive by annexation (iḍāfa); the two clauses are the maqūl al-qawl. ﴿فَلا﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction and lā is prohibitive. ﴿يُخْرِجَنَّكُما﴾ an imperfect verb indeclinable on the fatḥa because it is joined to the heavy nūn of emphasis, in the position of jussive by lā; its fāʿil is latent and the kāf is in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi. ﴿مِنَ الْجَنَّةِ﴾ attached to يخرجنكما; the clause is conjoined. ﴿فَتَشْقى﴾ the fāʾ is the fāʾ of causation (al-sababiyya), and تشقى is an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied (muḍmara) an after the fāʾ of causation; its fāʿil is latent; the implied an and the verb are interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun) conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:118-120.t: ﴿إِنَّ﴾ a particle resembling the verb. ﴿لَكَ﴾ [a preposition and its genitive noun] attached to (mutaʿalliq) the fronted khabar (predicate). ﴿إِنَّ﴾ a particle that makes the verb accusative. [Translator's note: the source writes ﴿إِنَّ﴾ here; the word in the verse is the an of أَلَّا (an + lā).] ﴿لا﴾ negative. ﴿تَجُوعَ﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an. ﴿فِيها﴾ attached to تجوع; the clause made of an and what follows it is interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of accusative as the postponed noun of inna. ﴿وَلا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction and lā is negative. ﴿تَعْرى﴾ conjoined to تجوع, accusative by the implied (muqaddara) fatḥa; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa). ﴿وَأَنَّكَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and anna and its noun. ﴿لا تَظْمَؤُا﴾ lā is negative; تظمأ is an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is the khabar of anna; anna, its noun and its khabar are interpreted as a maṣdar conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿فَوَسْوَسَ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction; وسوس is a past verb. ﴿إِلَيْهِ﴾ attached to وسوس. ﴿الشَّيْطانُ﴾ fāʿil; the clause is conjoined. ﴿قالَ﴾ the clause is explicative (tafsīriyya), with no position. ﴿يا آدَمُ﴾ yā is a vocative particle, and آدم is the one addressed (munādā), indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma; the clause is the maqūl al-qawl (object of the saying). ﴿هَلْ﴾ an interrogative particle. ﴿أَدُلُّكَ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; the kāf is in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿عَلى شَجَرَةِ﴾ attached to أدلك. ﴿الْخُلْدِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is the maqūl al-qawl. ﴿وَمُلْكٍ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction; ملك is conjoined to شجرة الخلد. ﴿لا يَبْلى﴾ lā is negative; يبلى is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma implied on its last letter; its fāʿil is latent; the clause is in the position of genitive as an adjective (ṣifa) of ملك.

daas-irab:121-123.t: ﴿فَأَكَلا﴾ the fāʾ is resumptive, and أكلا is a past verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa; the alif is the fāʿil (agent). ﴿مِنْها﴾ [a preposition and its genitive noun] attached to (mutaʿalliq) أكلا; the clause is resumptive. ﴿فَبَدَتْ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and بدت is a past verb; the tāʾ is the tāʾ of the feminine. ﴿لَهُما﴾ attached to بدت. ﴿سَوْآتُهُما﴾ fāʿil; the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa). ﴿وَطَفِقا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction; طفق is an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb and the alif is its noun. ﴿يَخْصِفانِ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn; the alif is the fāʿil; the clause is the khabar (predicate) of طفقا, and the clause طفقا is conjoined. ﴿عَلَيْهِما﴾ attached to يخصفان. ﴿مِنْ وَرَقِ﴾ attached to يخصفان. ﴿الْجَنَّةِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَعَصى﴾ the wāw is a conjunction; عصى is a past verb indeclinable on the implied (muqaddara) fatḥa. ﴿آدَمُ﴾ fāʿil. ﴿رَبَّهُ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿فَغَوى﴾ the clause is conjoined. ﴿ثُمَّ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿اجْتَباهُ﴾ a past verb and mafʿūl bihi. ﴿رَبُّهُ﴾ fāʿil; the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿فَتابَ﴾ the clause is conjoined. ﴿عَلَيْهِ﴾ attached to تاب. ﴿وَهَدى﴾ the clause is conjoined by the wāw. ﴿قالَ﴾ the clause is resumptive. ﴿اهْبِطا﴾ an imperative verb indeclinable on the deletion of the nūn; the alif is the fāʿil. ﴿مِنْها﴾ attached to اهبطا. ﴿جَمِيعاً﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿بَعْضُكُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject); the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿لِبَعْضٍ﴾ attached to عدو. ﴿عَدُوٌّ﴾ the khabar of بعضكم; the clause is in the position of accusative as ḥāl. ﴿فَإِمَّا﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction; immā is the conditional in with the redundant (zāʾida) mā. ﴿يَأْتِيَنَّكُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb indeclinable on the fatḥa because it is joined to the heavy nūn of emphasis; the kāf is mafʿūl bihi. ﴿مِنِّي﴾ attached to يأتينكم. ﴿هُدىً﴾ fāʿil. ﴿فَمَنِ﴾ the fāʾ links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). ﴿من﴾ conditional, mubtadaʾ. ﴿اتَّبَعَ﴾ the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), a past verb in the position of jussive; its fāʿil is latent (mustatir). ﴿هُدايَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the yāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ. ﴿فَلا﴾ the fāʾ links the apodosis and lā is negative. ﴿يَضِلُّ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is in the position of jussive as the apodosis. ﴿وَلا يَشْقى﴾ the wāw is a conjunction and lā is negative; the clause is conjoined. The clause ﴿فَمَنِ اتَّبَعَ﴾ is in the position of jussive as the apodosis of immā.

daas-irab:124-125.t: ﴿وَمَنْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and man is a jussive conditional noun, mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿أَعْرَضَ﴾ a past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿عَنْ ذِكْرِي﴾ [a preposition and its genitive noun] attached to (mutaʿalliq) أعرض. ﴿فَإِنَّ﴾ the fāʾ links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); inna is a particle resembling the verb. ﴿لَهُ﴾ attached to the fronted khabar (predicate). ﴿مَعِيشَةً﴾ its postponed noun. ﴿ضَنْكاً﴾ an adjective (ṣifa); the clause is in the position of jussive as the apodosis, and the two clauses of the condition and the apodosis are the khabar of the mubtadaʾ. The clause من … etc. is conjoined to the clause of the preceding apodosis, and its position is jussive like it. ﴿وَنَحْشُرُهُ﴾ the wāw is resumptive, and نحشر is an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is resumptive. ﴿يَوْمَ﴾ an adverb of time. ﴿الْقِيامَةِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the adverb is attached to نحشره. ﴿أَعْمى﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿قالَ﴾ the clause is resumptive. ﴿رَبِّ﴾ the one addressed (munādā) with an omitted vocative particle; رب is an accusative munādā because it is annexed to the omitted yāʾ of the first person. ﴿لِمَ﴾ the lām is a preposition, and mā is an interrogative noun whose alif was deleted to distinguish between the declarative and the interrogative, in the position of genitive by the lām; [the two are] attached to حشرتني. ﴿حَشَرْتَنِي﴾ a past verb, fāʿil and mafʿūl bihi; the nūn is for protection (wiqāya); the vocative clause and the one after it are the maqūl al-qawl (object of the saying). ﴿أَعْمى﴾ ḥāl. ﴿وَقَدْ﴾ the wāw is the wāw of circumstance (ḥāl) and qad is a particle of realisation (taḥqīq). ﴿كُنْتُ بَصِيراً﴾ kāna, its noun and its khabar; the clause is in the position of accusative as ḥāl.

farraa:1-1.t: His saying: ﴿طه﴾ is a letter of the alphabet. It has come in the exegesis that Ṭā-Hā means: "O man, O human being." Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us: Muḥammad narrated to us: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us: Qays ibn al-Rabīʿ narrated to me: ʿĀṣim narrated to me from Zirr ibn Ḥubaysh, who said: A man recited Ṭaha with fatḥa before Ibn Masʿūd. He said: ʿAbd Allāh said to him: "Ṭihi", with kasra. He said: The man said to him: "O Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, was he not simply commanded to tread with his foot [Translator's note: i.e. to set his feet on the ground]?" He said: He said to him: "Ṭihi. This is how the Messenger of Allah ﷺ taught me to recite it." Some of the readers used to separate it: Ṭi Hi. Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ read it "Ṭāhī", like this.

farraa:3-3.t: His saying: ﴿إِلاَّ تَذْكِرَةً﴾: he put it in the accusative on the basis of the sense: ﴿وَمَا أنزلناه إلا تذكرةً﴾ ("and We did not send it down except as a reminder").

farraa:4-4.t: His saying: ﴿تَنزِيلاً﴾: had it been (تنزيلٌ) (as a new beginning, istiʾnāf), it would have been correct.

farraa:7-7.t: His saying: ﴿يَعْلَمُ ٱلسِّرَّ﴾: what you have kept secret, (وَأَخْفَى): what you have said to yourself.

farraa:10-10.t:
His saying: ﴿إِنِّيۤ آنَسْتُ نَاراً﴾: I have found a fire. The Arabs say: "Go out and look around (fa-staʾnis): do you see anything?"
Among the proverbs of the Arabs: "بعد اطّلاع إيناس" (after looking out comes perceiving). Some of them say: "بعد طلوع إيناس".
His saying: ﴿لَّعَلِّيۤ آتِيكُمْ مِّنْهَا بِقَبَسٍ﴾: al-qabas is like fire at the tip of a stick or of a reed. His saying: ﴿أَوْ أَجِدُ عَلَى ٱلنَّارِ هُدًى﴾ means a guide (hādiyan); the maṣdar (verbal noun) took the place of "guide". Moses had lost his way.

farraa:11-12.t:
His saying: ﴿يٰمُوسَىٰ﴾ ﴿إِنِّيۤ﴾: if you make the calling fall on (موسى), you give kasra to ﴿إِنِّيۤ أَنَاْ رَبُّكَ﴾; and if you wish, you make the calling fall on (أَنِّى) as well as on (موسى); it has been read that way.
His saying: ﴿فَٱخْلَعْ نَعْلَيْكَ إِنَّكَ بِٱلْوَادِ ٱلْمُقَدَّسِ﴾: it is related that they were made of the hide of a dead donkey, so he was commanded to take them off [111 a] for that reason. His saying (طوَى): its ṭāʾ may be given kasra, and then it is declined fully (with tanwīn). The normal way of the speech is (full declension when the ṭāʾ has kasra); but if you make it a name for what lies around the valley, it may be left undeclined, just as it was said ﴿وَيَوْمَ حُنَيْنٍ إذْ أَعْجَبَتْكُمْ﴾, where they declined Ḥunayn fully, because it is the name of the valley. And the poet said, leaving it undeclined:
نصروا نبيَّهُمُ وشدُّوا أَزْره * بحُنَينَ يوم تواكُلِ الأبطال
(They helped their Prophet and strengthened his back at Ḥunayn on the day when the heroes left the fighting to one another.)
He intended to make (Ḥunayn) the name of the territory [Translator's note: the text has «للبدة», evidently for «للبلدة»], so he did not decline it fully. And another said:
ألَسْنَا أكرم الثقلين رَحْلا * وأعظمه ببَطن حِرَاء نارَا
(Are we not the noblest of men and jinn in dwelling, and the greatest of them in fire in the hollow of Ḥirāʾ?)
He did not decline Ḥirāʾ fully — it is a mountain — because he made it the name of the territory in which it lies.
As for whoever gives ḍamma to (طُوى), full declension predominates for it; yet it may be left undeclined by treating it as having the pattern fuʿal, like Zufar, ʿUmar and Muḍar. Al-Farrāʾ said: it is read (طُوًى), fully declined.

farraa:13-13.t: His saying: ﴿وَأَنَا ٱخْتَرْتُكَ﴾: it is also read [وأَنَّا اخترناكَ], referred back to [نودى]: "He was called: that We have chosen you"; and "Innā ikhtarnāka": when one gives it kasra, one makes it a new beginning.

farraa:14-14.t:
His saying: ﴿وَأَقِمِ ٱلصَّلاَةَ لِذِكْرِيۤ﴾: it is also read (لِذِكْرَا) with alif. Whoever says (ذِكْرَا), making it with alif, takes it in the sense of al-dhikrā ("remembrance"). Or, if you wish, you make it the yāʾ of the first-person possessive turned into alif for the sake of the verse-endings, as the poet said:
أطوِّف ما أطوِّف ثم آوِى * إِلى أُمَّا ويُروِينى النقيعِ
(I roam about as much as I roam, then I return to my mother, and the steeped drink quenches my thirst.)
The Arabs say "بأبا وأُمَّا", meaning "بأبى وأُمِّي" ("by my father and my mother"). Similar to it is ﴿يا وَيْلَتَا - أَعَجَزتُ﴾: if you wish you make it the possessive yāʾ, and if you wish the yāʾ of lamentation (nudba); and ﴿يا حَسْرَتَا عَلَى مَا فَرَّطْتُ فىِ جَنْبِ اللهِ﴾.

farraa:15-15.t:
[His saying: ﴿أَكَادُ أُخْفِيهَا﴾: the readers read (أكاد أُخفيها) with ḍamma. In the reading of Ubayy: (إن السّاعة آتِيَة أكاد أُخفيها من نفسى فكيف أُظهركم عليها} ("the Hour is coming; I almost hide it from Myself, so how should I disclose it to you?"). Saʿīd ibn Jubayr read (أَخْفِيها) with fatḥa on the alif. Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us: Muḥammad narrated to us: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us: al-Kisāʾī narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn Sahl from Waqāʾ from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr that he read (أَخفيَها) with fatḥa on the alif, from khafaytu. Khafaytu means "I made manifest", and khafaytu means "I concealed". Al-Farrāʾ said: al-Kisāʾī said, and the jurists say [Translator's note: the sentence breaks off in the source]. The poet said:
فإن تدفنوا الداء لا نخفِه * وإن تبعثوا الحرب لا نَقْعُدِ
(If you bury the malady, we will not bring it to light; and if you stir up war, we will not sit idle.)
He means: we will not make it manifest.
[Translator's note: the bracketing of this entry is unbalanced in the source and is reproduced as written.]

farraa:16-16.t: His saying: ﴿فَلاَ يَصُدَّنَّكَ عَنْهَا﴾: He means faith; and it is said: from the Hour, i.e. from its coming. It is permissible to say "from it" (feminine) while you mean faith, just as He said ﴿ثُمَّ إنّ رَبَّكَ لِلَّذِينَ هَاجَرُوا﴾ and then said ﴿إنَّ رَبَّكَ مِنْ بَعْدِهَا لَغَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾, taking it to refer to the deed (al-faʿla).

farraa:17-17.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمَا تِلْكَ بِيَمِينِكَ يٰمُوسَىٰ﴾ means his staff, and the meaning of (تلك) is "this".
His saying: ﴿بِيَمِينِكَ﴾ is, in one view, a ṣila (relative clause) of tilka, because tilka and hādhihi can take a ṣila just as alladhī does. The poet said:
عَدَسْ ما لِعبَّاد عليكِ إمارة * أمِنتِ وهّذَا تحملين طليقُ
(ʿAdas! ʿAbbād has no authority over you; you are safe, and this one whom you carry is free.)
ʿAdas is a call to urge on a mule. He means: the one whom you carry is free.

farraa:18-18.t: His saying: ﴿وَأَهُشُّ بِهَا عَلَىٰ غَنَمِي﴾: I strike the dry trees with it so that their leaves fall, and his sheep graze on them. ﴿وَلِيَ فِيهَا مَآرِبُ أُخْرَىٰ﴾ means needs. He made ukhrā a naʿt (adjective) of maʾārib, which is a plural. Had He said ukhar, it would have been permissible, as Allah said ﴿فَعِدَّة مِنْ أَيَّامٍ أُخَر﴾; and similar to it is ﴿وَلِلّهِ الأسْمَاءُ الحُسْنَى﴾.

farraa:21-21.t: His saying: ﴿سِيَرتَهَا ٱلأُولَىٰ﴾: that is, its former state. He is saying: He will return it to a staff as it was.

farraa:22-22.t:
His saying: ﴿وَٱضْمُمْ يَدَكَ إِلَىٰ جَنَاحِكَ﴾: al-janāḥ in this place is from the bottom of the upper arm to the armpit.
His saying: ﴿تَخْرُجْ بَيْضَآءَ مِنْ غَيْرِ سُوۤءٍ﴾: that is, leprosy [Translator's note: i.e. without leprosy].
His saying: ﴿آيَةً أُخْرَىٰ﴾: the meaning is "it is another sign" and "this is another sign"; since neither hiya nor hādhihi was brought before āya, it became joined to the verb and was put in the accusative.

farraa:23-23.t: His saying: ﴿مِنْ آيَاتِنَا ٱلْكُبْرَىٰ﴾: had it been said al-kubar, it would have been correct; it is on a par with (al-asmāʾ al-ḥusnā) and (maʾārib ukhrā).

farraa:27-27.t: His saying: ﴿وَٱحْلُلْ عُقْدَةً مِّن لِّسَانِي﴾: there was a stammer (rutta) in his tongue.

farraa:30-30.t:
His saying: ﴿هَارُونَ أَخِي﴾: if you wish, you make (اجعل) fall on (Hārūna akhī) and make al-wazīr its object [Translator's note: the text has «فعلا له», literally "a verb for it"; probably «مفعولا له», "an object for it", is meant]. And if you wish, you make (Hārūna akhī) an explanation of al-wazīr, so it is accusative by repetition (al-takrīr). In (هارون) the nominative is also permissible as a new beginning (al-iʾtināf), because it is a definite noun explaining an indefinite one, as the poet said:
فإن لها جَارين لن يَغدِرا بها * رَبيبُ النبىّ وابنُ خير الخَلاَئِق
(For she has two protectors who will never betray her: the Prophet's stepson and the son of the best of creatures.)

farraa:31-31.t: His saying: ﴿ٱشْدُدْ بِهِ﴾ is a supplication: "(Strengthen by him), O Lord, (my back, and make him share), O Lord, (in my affair)" — a supplication from Moses. In one of the two readings it is ﴿أَشْدُدْ بِهِ أزْرِى وأُشْرِكْه فى أَمرى﴾ with ḍamma on the alif. It is reported from al-Ḥasan: ﴿أَشْدُدْ به﴾ as a jussive response (jazāʾ) to the supplication, because of His saying ﴿اجعل لى﴾, and ﴿وأُشْرِكه﴾ with ḍamma on the alif in (أشركه), because it is an act of Moses.

farraa:37-37.t: His saying: ﴿وَلَقَدْ مَنَنَّا عَلَيْكَ مَرَّةً أُخْرَىٰ﴾: before this one. It is the kindness shown to him when he fell into Pharaoh's hands, so that He made him beloved to them until they nourished him. That is the other favour (along with this verse).

farraa:38-40.t:
And He explained it when He said: ﴿ إِذْ أَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَىٰ أُمِّكَ مَا يُوحَىٰ﴾ ﴿أَنِ ٱقْذِفِيهِ فِي ٱلتَّابُوتِ فَٱقْذِفِيهِ فِي ٱلْيَمِّ﴾, then He said: ﴿فَلْيُلْقِهِ ٱلْيَمُّ بِٱلسَّاحِلِ﴾: this is a conditional response (jazāʾ) cast in the form of a command, as though the sea were commanded. It is like His saying: ﴿اتَّبِعُوا سَبِيلَنَا وَلْنَحْمِلْ﴾, the meaning — and Allah knows best — being: "Follow our way and we will carry your sins for you." Likewise Allah promised her: "Cast him into the sea, and the sea will cast him onto the shore." It is related that the sea cast him to the watering-place of Pharaoh's family, and his slave girls carried him to his wife.
His saying: ﴿وَأَلْقَيْتُ عَلَيْكَ مَحَبَّةً مِّنِّي﴾: he was made beloved to (everyone who saw him).
His saying: ﴿وَلِتُصْنَعَ عَلَىٰ عَيْنِيۤ﴾ ﴿إِذْ تَمْشِيۤ أُخْتُكَ فَتَقُولُ﴾: He mentioned the walking alone, and did not mention that she walked until she came in to Pharaoh's family and directed them to the wet-nurse. There is much like this in the Revelation, such as His saying: ﴿أَنَا أُنَبِّئُكُمْ بِتَأوِيِله فَأَرْسِلُونِ يُوسُفُ﴾, and He did not say "so he was sent, and he entered and said: Joseph". It is part of the speech of the Arabs to make do (with omitting much) of the speech and with little of it when the meaning is known.
His saying: ﴿وَفَتَنَّاكَ فُتُوناً﴾: We tried you with distress — the distress of the killing — as a trial.
His saying: ﴿عَلَىٰ قَدَرٍ يٰمُوسَىٰ﴾: He means: according to what Allah willed of speaking to him.

farraa:42-42.t: His saying: ﴿وَلاَ تَنِيَا﴾: He means: do not weaken and do not slacken. "ʿan dhikrī" and "fī dhikrī" are the same.

farraa:44-44.t: His saying: ﴿قَوْلاً لَّيِّناً﴾: Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us: Muḥammad narrated to us: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us: Muḥammad ibn Abān al-Qurashī narrated to me; he said: they addressed him by his kunya. Muḥammad ibn Abān said: he was given the kunya Abū Murra. Al-Farrāʾ said: and it is said: Abū al-Walīd.

farraa:45-45.t: His saying: ﴿أَن يَفْرُطَ عَلَيْنَآ﴾, and (يُفْرِط): He means in hastening to punish us. The Arabs say: faraṭa minhu amrun ("something escaped him hastily"); afraṭa: he went to excess; and farraṭa: he fell short and forgot.

farraa:47-47.t:
His saying: ﴿إِنَّا رَسُولاَ رَبِّكَ﴾: "rasūlu rabbika" (singular) is also permissible, because rasūl may be used for a plural, a dual and a singular. The poet said:
أَلِكْنِى إليها وخير الرسو * ل أعلمهم بنواحى الخبَرْ
(Be my messenger to her; and the best of messengers is the one who knows best the sides of the news.)
He meant: messengers (al-rusul).
His saying: ﴿وَٱلسَّلاَمُ عَلَىٰ مَنِ ٱتَّبَعَ ٱلْهُدَىٰ﴾: He means safety be upon whoever follows the guidance; "ʿalā man" and "li-man" are the same. (He said: Moses was commanded to say to Pharaoh: "And peace be upon whoever follows the guidance.")

farraa:48-48.t: His saying: ﴿إِنَّا قَدْ أُوحِيَ إِلَيْنَآ أَنَّ ٱلْعَذَابَ عَلَىٰ مَن كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ﴾ is evidence for the meaning of His saying: whoever follows the guidance will be safe.

farraa:49-49.t:
His saying: ﴿قَالَ فَمَن رَّبُّكُمَا يٰمُوسَىٰ﴾: he speaks to the two and then directs the address to one, because speech comes from one, not from the group. Similar to it, of cases where the act is ascribed to two while it belongs to one, is His saying: ﴿نسِيَا حُوتَهُمَا﴾, while only one of them forgot it; do you not see that he said to Moses ﴿فَإنِّي نَسيِتُ الحُوتَ﴾? And similar to it is ﴿يَخْرُجُ مِنْهُمَا الُّلؤْلؤُ والمَرْجَانُ﴾, while they come out only from the salt [Translator's note: i.e. the salt sea].
His saying: ﴿أَعْطَى كُلَّ شَىءٍ خَلْقَهْ﴾ [it is said: He gave the male among people a woman like him, of his own kind; the ram a ewe, and the bull a cow.]

farraa:50-50.t: His saying: ﴿ثُمَّ هَدَىٰ﴾: He inspired the male the approach [Translator's note: i.e. how the male comes to the female].

farraa:52-52.t: His saying: ﴿فِي كِتَابٍ لاَّ يَضِلُّ رَبِّي﴾: rabbī, i.e. He does not forget it. (رَبّى) is in the position of the nominative; you imply the hāʾ in yaḍilluhu, (وَلاَ يَنسَى). You say aḍlaltu the thing when it is lost, such as a she-camel, a horse, or whatever gets away from you. When you miss a thing whose place is fixed, such as a house or a place, you say ḍalaltuhu and ḍaliltuhu — two dialectal forms — and you do not say aḍlaltu or aḍlaltuhu.

farraa:53-53.t: His saying: ﴿زْوَاجاً مِّن نَّبَاتٍ شَتَّىٰ﴾: differing in colours and tastes.

farraa:54-54.t: His saying: ﴿إِنَّ فِي ذٰلِكَ لآيَاتٍ لأُوْلِي ٱلنُّهَىٰ﴾: He is saying: in the difference of its colours and its taste there are signs for people of intellect. You say of a man: "innahu la-dhū nuhya" when he has intellect.

farraa:55-55.t: His saying: ﴿تَارَةً أُخْرَىٰ﴾ is referred back to His saying ﴿مِنْهَا خَلَقْنَاكُمْ﴾, not to (نُعِيدُكُمْ), because ukhrā and ākhar refer back only to their like. You say in speech: "I bought a she-camel, a house and another she-camel", so (ukhrā) refers back to the she-camel, which is its like, and it is not permissible for it (to refer back) to the house. Likewise His saying ﴿مِنْهَا خَلَقْنَاكُمْ﴾ is like saying ﴿مِنْهَا أخْرجناكم، ونخرجكم بعد الموت (مرة أخرى)﴾ ("from it We brought you out, and We will bring you out after death another time").

farraa:58-58.t: His saying: ﴿فَٱجْعَلْ بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَكَ مَوْعِداً﴾: he is saying: "Set a term between us", so he set it. His saying: ﴿مَكَاناً سُوًى﴾, and (سِوَى): most of the speech of the Arabs is sawāʾ, with fatḥa and the long vowel, when it has the meaning of "midway" and "fair"; they give it fatḥa and lengthen it, as in Allah's saying ﴿تعالوا إلَى كلِمَةٍ سَوَاءٍ بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَكُمْ﴾. The kasra and the ḍamma with the short vowel are both good Arabic, and they occur only in the short form; it has been read with both.

farraa:59-59.t:
His saying: ﴿يَوْمُ ٱلزِّينَةِ﴾: it is related that he made their appointment a festival day; and it is said: a market day they used to have, on which they adorned themselves.
His saying: ﴿وَأَن يُحْشَرَ ٱلنَّاسُ ضُحًى﴾: he is saying: when you see the people gathered from every direction in the forenoon, that is the appointment. The position of (أن) is nominative, referred back to al-yawm, or genitive, referred back to al-zīna, i.e. "the day on which the people are gathered".

farraa:61-61.t:
His saying: ﴿فَيُسْحِتَكُم﴾: saḥata is more common; it is uprooting entirely: He will uproot you with a punishment. Al-Farazdaq said:
وعَض زمان يابنَ مرَوانَ لم يَدعْ * من المال إلاّ مُسْحَتاً أو مُجَلَّف
(And the bite of a time, O son of Marwān, that left of wealth nothing but what was wiped out or stripped bare.)
The Arabs say saḥata and asḥata with one meaning. He [Translator's note: the transmitter] said: It was said to al-Farrāʾ: "Some of the transmitters say: mā bihi min al-māli illā musḥatun aw mujallaf." He said: "That is nothing." Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us: Muḥammad narrated to us: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us: Abū Jaʿfar al-Ruʾāsī narrated to me from Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ, who said: Al-Farazdaq passed by ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Isḥāq al-Ḥaḍramī, the grammarian, and recited this ode to him:
عَزَفتَ بأعشاش وما كدت تعزِف
(You turned away at Aʿshāsh, though you had hardly been about to turn away)
until he reached this verse...
وعَضُّ زمان يابن مروان لَم يَدَعْ * من المال إلاّ مُسْحَت أو مُجَلَّف
(And the bite of a time, O son of Marwān, did not leave anything of wealth; what remains is only the wiped out or the stripped bare.)
So ʿAbd Allāh said to al-Farazdaq: "On what basis did you put it in the nominative?" Al-Farazdaq said to him: "On what will annoy you."

farraa:62-62.t: His saying: ﴿فَتَنَازَعُوۤاْ أَمْرَهُمْ بَيْنَهُمْ﴾ means the sorcerers. Some of them said to others: "If Moses defeats us, we will follow him", and they kept it secret from Pharaoh and his companions.

farraa:63-63.t:
His saying: ﴿إِنْ هَـٰذَانِ لَسَاحِرَانِ﴾: the readers have differed over it. Some of them said: it is a grammatical error (laḥn), but we let it stand so as not to contradict the written text. Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us: Muḥammad narrated to us: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us: Abū Muʿāwiya al-Ḍarīr narrated to me from Hāshim ibn ʿUrwa ibn al-Zubayr from his father from ʿĀʾisha that she was asked about His saying in al-Nisāʾ ﴿لَكِنِ الراسِخُونَ فىِ العِلْمِ مِنْهمْ .... والمُقِيمِينَ الصلاةَ﴾, about His saying in al-Māʾida ﴿إِنَ الذِينَ آمَنوا والّذِين هَادُوا والصَّابِئُونَ﴾, and about His saying ﴿إِنَّ هَذَانِ لَسَاحِرَانِ﴾, and she said: "O son of my brother, this was an error of the scribe." [Translator's note: the name is given as «هاشم بن عروة»; the well-known transmitter from ʿUrwa is his son Hishām.] Abū ʿAmr read ﴿إنَّ هَذَيْنِ لَساحِرَان﴾, and argued that it had reached him from one of the Companions of Muḥammad ﷺ that he said: "There is a grammatical error in the Muṣḥaf, and the Arabs will set it right."
Al-Farrāʾ said: I do not like (to contradict the written text) [Translator's note: the parenthesis opened here is not closed in the source]. Some of them read (إنْ هَذَان لساحران) with the light form [Translator's note: of in]. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: (وأسروا النجوى أَن هذان ساحران), and in the reading of Ubayy: (إنْ ذان إلاّ ساحران). Our reading, with the doubled (إنّ) and with the alif, has two explanations.
One of them is according to the dialect of the Banū al-Ḥārith ibn Kaʿb: they render the dual with alif in the nominative, accusative and genitive alike. A man of the Asd recited to me from them — he meant the Banū al-Ḥārith:
فأَطرق إطراق الشجاع ولو يرى * مَسَاغاً لِناباه الشجاعُ لصَمّما
(He lowered his head as the serpent lowers its head; and had the serpent seen a way in for its two fangs, it would have bitten deep.)
He said: I have never seen anyone more eloquent than this man of the Asd. This man also related from them: "This is the handwriting of my brother's two hands (yadā akhī) itself." That — even if it is rare — is more consistent with analogy (aqyas), because the Arabs said muslimūna, making the wāw follow the ḍamma (since the wāw does not take case vowels), and then said raʾaytu al-muslimīna, making the yāʾ follow the kasra of the mīm. When they saw that, with the yāʾ of the dual, they could not give kasra to what precedes it, and it remained with fatḥa, they left the alif to follow it, and said rajulān in every case. The Arabs have agreed on keeping the alif in kilā al-rajulayn in the nominative, accusative and genitive, though they refer to two — except the Banū Kināna, who say "raʾaytu kilay al-rajulayn" and "marartu bi-kilay al-rajulayn"; that is ugly and rare; they followed analogy.
The other explanation is that you say: I found the alif (of hādhā to be a prop (diʿāma) and not the final radical of the word; so when I made it dual I added a nūn to it and then left the alif) fixed in its state, not changing in any case; just as the Arabs said (الذى) and then added a nūn indicating the plural and said alladhīna in their nominative, accusative and genitive, just as they left (hādhān) in its nominative, accusative and genitive. Kināna say (اللَّذُونَ).
His saying: ﴿وَيَذْهَبَا بِطَرِيقَتِكُمُ ٱلْمُثْلَىٰ﴾: al-ṭarīqa is the noble men. His saying (المثلى) means al-amthal: they will take away your nobles. He said al-muthlā and did not say al-muthul, like (al-asmāʾ al-ḥusnā). If you wish, you make (al-muthlā) feminine because al-ṭarīqa is feminine. The Arabs say of a people: "These are the ṭarīqa of their people" and "the ṭarāʾiq of their people", meaning their nobles; and His saying ﴿كُنَّا طَرَائِقَ قِدَداً﴾ is from that. They also say of a single person: "This is the ṭarīqa of his people" and "the naẓūra of his people" — and some of them "the naẓīra of his people" — and they say of a group, with the singular and the plural: "These are the naẓūra of their people" and "the naẓāʾir of their people".

farraa:64-64.t:
His saying: ﴿فَأَجْمِعُواْ كَيْدَكُمْ﴾: al-ijmāʿ is making firm and resolving upon [113 a] a thing. You say ajmaʿtu al-khurūja and ʿalā al-khurūji ("I resolved to go out"), like azmaʿtu. The poet said:
يا ليت شعرى والمنى لا تنفع * هل أَغدُوَنْ يوماً وأمرى مُجْمَع
(Would that I knew — and wishes do not avail — whether I shall set out one day with my affair resolved.)
He means: it has been made firm and resolved upon. Whoever reads (فأجْمَعُوا) is saying: do not leave out anything of your plotting, but bring it all.
His saying ﴿مَنِ ٱسْتَعْلَىٰ﴾: whoever prevails.

farraa:65-65.t:
His saying: ﴿إِمَّآ أَن تُلْقِيَ وَإِمَّآ أَن نَّكُونَ أَوَّلَ مَنْ أَلْقَىٰ﴾: (أَن) is in the position of the accusative, the meaning being "choose one of these two". Had it been put in the nominative, since the verb is not overt, it would have been correct, as though it were a statement, as in the poet's saying:
فسِيرا فإمَّا حاجةٌ تقضِيانها * وإمَّا مقِيلٌ صَالح وصَديق
(So travel on, you two: either there is a need you will fulfil, or a good resting-place and a friend.)
Had His saying ﴿فإمَّا مَنٌّ بَعْدُ وإمَّا فَدِاءٌ﴾ been put in the nominative, that too would have been correct, its approach being like that of His saying ﴿فَإمْساكٌ بِمَعرُوفٍ أَو تَسْريحٌ بإحْسَانٍ﴾. The accusative in His saying ﴿ إمَّا أَنْ تُلْقِىَ﴾ and in His saying ﴿فإمَّا مَنّاً بَعْدُ وإمَّا فَدِاءً﴾ is better than the nominative, because it is something that is not general — unlike what you see of the meaning of His saying ﴿فإمْسَاكٌ﴾ and ﴿فَصِيَامُ ثلاَثَةِ أيَّامٍ﴾: since the meaning there covers all people, in retaining honourably and in fasting three days in the expiation of an oath, it was like a conditional response (jazāʾ) and was put in the nominative for that reason; whereas the choosing is only a single act. The meaning of (أفلح) [Translator's note: in 20:64] is: he lived and was saved.

farraa:66-66.t: His saying: ﴿يُخَيَّلُ إِلَيْهِ مِن سِحْرِهِمْ أَنَّهَا تَسْعَىٰ﴾: (أنَّها) is in the position of the nominative. Whoever reads (تُخَيِّلُ) or (تَخَيَّلُ), it is in the position of the accusative, because the meaning is "it takes on an appearance, to them, by moving", and "it gives an impression" likewise; when you drop the bāʾ you put it in the accusative, just as you say "aradtu bi-an aqūma", whose meaning is "I wanted to stand"; when you drop the bāʾ you put it in the accusative. Allah said ﴿وَمَنْ يُرِدْ فِيهِ بإِلحَادٍ بِظُلْمٍ﴾; had you dropped the bāʾ you would have put it in the accusative and said: "wa-man yurid fīhi ilḥādan bi-ẓulmin".

farraa:69-69.t:
His saying: ﴿إِنَّمَا صَنَعُواْ كَيْدُ سَاحِرٍ﴾: you make (ما) take the role of alladhī: "Indeed, what they have made is the plot of sorcery"; some of them have read it ﴿كَيدُ سَاحِرٍ﴾, and all is correct. Had you put ﴿ كَيْدَ سحر﴾ in the accusative, it would have been correct, making (إنما) a single particle, like His saying ﴿إنَّما تَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللّهِ أَوْثَانَا﴾.
His saying: ﴿وَلاَ يُفْلِحُ ٱلسَّاحِرُ حَيْثُ أَتَىٰ﴾: it has come in the exegesis that he is to be killed wherever he is found.

farraa:71-71.t:
His saying: ﴿فَلأُقَطِّعَنَّ أَيْدِيَكُمْ وَأَرْجُلَكُمْ مِّنْ خِلاَفٍ﴾: in such speech ʿan, ʿalā and bāʾ are also suitable.
His saying ﴿وَلأُصَلِّبَنَّكُمْ فِي جُذُوعِ ٱلنَّخْلِ﴾: (على) is suitable in place of (فى). (فى) is suitable because he is raised up in the wood along its length, so (فى) is suitable; and (عَلى) is suitable because he is raised up in it and so comes to be on it. Allah has said ﴿وَاتَّبَعُوا مَا تَتْلُو الشَّيَاطِينُ عَلَى مُلْكِ سُلَيْمان﴾, and its meaning is "in the reign of Solomon". His saying ﴿أَشَدُّ عَذَاباً وَأَبْقَىٰ﴾: He is saying: and more lasting.

farraa:72-72.t:
His saying: ﴿قَالُواْ لَن نُّؤْثِرَكَ عَلَىٰ مَا جَآءَنَا مِنَ ٱلْبَيِّنَاتِ وَٱلَّذِي فَطَرَنَا﴾: alladhī is in the position of the genitive: "and over the One who". Had they meant by their saying (والذى فطرنا) an oath by it, it would have been genitive and would have been correct, as though they said: "We will not prefer you, by Allah."
His saying ﴿فَٱقْضِ مَآ أَنتَ قَاضٍ﴾: do whatever you will. His saying ﴿إِنَّمَا تَقْضِي هَـٰذِهِ ٱلْحَيَاةَ ٱلدُّنْيَآ﴾: innamā is a single particle; for that reason you put (al-ḥayāh) in the accusative. Had a reader read (al-ḥayāh) in the nominative, it would have been permissible, making (مَا) take the role of alladhī, as though he said: "What you decree is this worldly [Translator's note: life]."

farraa:73-73.t: His saying: ﴿وَمَآ أَكْرَهْتَنَا عَلَيْهِ مِنَ ٱلسِّحْرِ﴾: mā is in the position of the accusative, referred back to the sense of al-khaṭāyā ("the sins"). It is mentioned in the exegesis that Pharaoh had forced the sorcerers [113 b] to learn sorcery.

farraa:77-77.t:
His saying: ﴿لاَّ تَخَافُ دَرَكاً وَلاَ تَخْشَىٰ﴾ is nominative as a new beginning (istiʾnāf) with lā, as He said ﴿وَأْمُرْ أَهْلَكَ بِالصَّلاَةِ وَاصْطَبِرْ عَلَيْهَا لاَ نَسْأَلُكَ رِزْقََا﴾; most of what has come in response to a command with lā is in the nominative. Ḥamza read (لا تَخَفْ دَرَكاً), putting it in the jussive as a conditional response (jazāʾ), and put (وَلاَ تَخْشَىٰ) in the nominative as a new beginning, as He said ﴿يُوَلُّوكُمُ الأَدْبَارَ ثُمَّ لاَ يُنْصَرُونَ﴾, beginning anew with thumma; this is like it. Had Ḥamza intended the jussive in His saying ﴿وَلاَ تَخْشَىٰ﴾, even though it has the yāʾ [Translator's note: i.e. the final long vowel], it would have been correct, as the poet said:
* هُزِّى إليك الجِذُع يجنيك الجَنَى *
(Shake the trunk towards you, and it will yield you fresh fruit.)
and he did not say yajnik al-janā. Another said:
هجوتَ زَبَّان ثمَّ جئتَ معتذِراً * من سَبّ زَبَّان لم تهجو ولم تَدِعِ
(You satirized Zabbān, then came apologizing for reviling Zabbān — as if you had not satirized and had not let it be.)
And another said:
أَلَمْ يَأتِيكَ والأَنباءُ تَنْمِى * بِمَا لاَقت لَبُونُ بنى زِيادِ
(Has it not reached you — and news spreads — what the milch-camels of the Banū Ziyād met with?)
He kept the yāʾ in (يأتيك) while it is in the position of the jussive, because of its being quiescent, and so that was permissible.

farraa:81-81.t: His saying: ﴿فَيَحِلَّ عَلَيْكُمْ غَضَبِي﴾: the kasra in it is dearer to me than the ḍamma, because al-ḥulūl (with yaḥullu) is what actually befalls, while yaḥillu means "becomes due"; and the exegesis has come with "becoming due", not with "befalling". All is correct, if Allah wills. Al-Kisāʾī took it in the sense of befalling. In the reading of al-Farrāʾ it is with ḍamma, like al-Kisāʾī; he was asked about it and said so [Translator's note: this sentence appears to be a transmitter's remark and reads awkwardly in the source]. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh or Ubayy, ﴿إن شاء الله﴾ ﴿وَلاَ يحُلَّنَّ عَلَيْكُمُ غَضَبِى وَمَنْ يَحْلُلْ عَلَيْه﴾, with ḍamma. As for His saying ﴿أَمْ أَرَدْتُمْ أَنْ يَحِلَّ عَلَيْكُمُ﴾, it is with kasra, and it is like the two preceding ones; had it been given ḍamma it would have been correct. When you say "ḥalla bihim al-ʿadhāb" ("the punishment descended upon them"), it is yaḥullu with ḍamma and nothing else; and when you say ʿalā, or you say "yaḥillu laka such-and-such" ("such-and-such is lawful for you"), it is with kasra.

farraa:82-82.t: His saying: ﴿ثُمَّ ٱهْتَدَىٰ﴾: he knew that there is reward and punishment for that.

farraa:84-84.t: His saying: ﴿قَالَ هُمْ أُوْلاۤءِ عَلَىٰ أَثَرِي﴾: some of the readers have read (أُولاىَ عَلَى أَثَرِى), dropping the hamza; and when the hamza is dropped it is made to resemble the possessive form, just as Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb read ﴿مِلّة آباىَ إبراهيمَ﴾ and ﴿وَتَقَبَّل دُعَاىَ رَبَّنَا﴾.

farraa:87-87.t:
His saying: ﴿مَآ أَخْلَفْنَا مَوْعِدَكَ بِمَلْكِنَا﴾ with ḍamma on the mīm [Translator's note: the printed Quranic text in this entry is vowelled «بِمَلْكِنَا» with fatḥa]. (This is the reading of the readers.) Had it been read bi-milkinā (and bi-malkinā), it would have been correct. The meaning of (mulkinā) in the exegesis is: we were not in control of what was right; we simply erred.
His saying ﴿وَلَـٰكِنَّا حُمِّلْنَآ أَوْزَاراً مِّن زِينَةِ ٱلْقَوْمِ﴾ means the gold, silver and iron they had taken from Pharaoh's people when the sea cast them out; "so we threw it into the fire, and al-Sāmirī did likewise, and we followed him." When the silver and the gold of what they had thrown became pure, al-Sāmirī fashioned it into a calf. He had taken a handful from the track of a horse that was under Gabriel. (Al-Sāmirī said to Moses: "It was cast into my mind that if I threw that handful on something dead it would come to life"; so he threw that handful into the nose of the bull and into its rear, and it came to life and lowed.) Al-Farrāʾ said: In the exegesis of al-Kalbī, the horse was [Translator's note: the horse of] life [Translator's note: the text reads «أن الفرس كانت الحياة»]. That is His saying ﴿وكَذَلكَ سَوَّلَتْ لِى نَفْسِى﴾: he is saying, my soul made it seem attractive to me.
Whoever reads bi-milkinā with kasra on the mīm, it is al-milk, what a man owns; you say of anything you own: "This is milk yamīnī (the property of my right hand)", of a slave and of other things that are owned. Al-malk is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of malaktuhu malkan and malakatan, like ghalabtuhu ghalban and ghalabatan. Al-mulk is sovereignty. Some of the Banū Asad say "mā lī mulk", meaning: I have nothing I own. Milk al-ṭarīq and malkuhu is its middle (wajh). The poet said:
أقامت على مَلْك الطريق فَمَلكه * لها ولمَنكوب المطايا جَوانبهُ
(She kept to the middle of the road: its middle is hers, and its sides belong to the footsore mounts.)
[114 a] Along with malk al-ṭarīq it is also said: fa-milkuhu. [Translator's note: One says:] she kept to the bulk (ʿuẓm) of the road, to the smooth part (sujuḥ) of the road, and to its course (sanan and sunan).

farraa:88-88.t: His saying: ﴿فَنَسِيَ﴾ means that Moses forgot: he missed the way and was slow in returning to them, so they took up the calf; and Allah reproached them, saying: Do they not see that the calf does not speak and has no power to harm or benefit them?

farraa:96-96.t: His saying: ﴿فَقَبَضْتُ قَبْضَةً﴾: al-qabḍa is with the whole hand, and al-qabṣa is with the fingertips. Al-Ḥasan read qabṣa with ṣād. Al-qubṣa and al-qubḍa (with ḍamma) are both the name of the earth itself [Translator's note: that is taken]; had they been read, it would have been a valid option. Similar to it, among what has been read, is ﴿إلاَّ مَنِ اغترف غُرْفة بيده﴾ and (غَرْفَةً): al-ghurfa is what is scooped up, and al-gharfa is the single act. Likewise al-ḥuswa and al-ḥaswa, al-khuṭwa and al-khaṭwa, al-ukla and al-akla: al-ukla is what is eaten and al-akla is the single time; al-khuṭwa is the distance between the feet in walking and al-khaṭwa is the single time. What has kasra is a maṣdar (of manner), as in "he has a fine way of walking (al-mishya), sitting (al-jilsa) and sitting down (al-qiʿda)".

farraa:97-97.t:
His saying: ﴿فَإِنَّ لَكَ فِي ٱلْحَيَاةِ أَن تَقُولَ لاَ مِسَاسَ﴾: that is, "I am not to be touched and I do not touch." The interpretation of that is that Moses commanded them not to eat with him, not to mix with him and not to trade with him. It is also read (لا مَسَاسِ), which is a widespread dialectal form: "lā masāsi, lā masāsi", like nazāli and naẓāri, from al-intiẓār ("waiting"). His saying ﴿الذِى ظَلْت عليه عاكفاً﴾ and ﴿ظِلْت﴾, and ﴿فَظَلتُم تفكَّهُوَن﴾ and ﴿فَظِلتم﴾: fatḥa and kasra are both permissible only because their meaning is ẓaliltum, and the first lām has been dropped. Whoever gives kasra to the ẓāʾ puts the kasra of the dropped lām on the ẓāʾ; and whoever gives fatḥa to the ẓāʾ says: it had fatḥa, so I left it with its fatḥa. Similar to it are masastu and masistu: the Arabs say "qad mastu that" and "mistuhu"; "hamamtu bi-dhālika" and "hamtu"; and "wadidtu" and "wadadtu" [Translator's note: the words «كذا فى ب» ("thus in manuscript B") stand in the text here] "that you had done that"; and "hal aḥsasta ṣāḥibaka?" and "hal aḥasta?" ("did you perceive your companion?").
His saying ﴿لَّنُحَرِّقَنَّهُ﴾ — with fire — and ﴿لَنَحرُقَنَّه﴾: we will file it down with iron, from ḥaraqtu, aḥruquhu and aḥriquhu, two dialectal forms. Al-Mufaḍḍal recited to me:
بذى فَرِقَيْنِ يوم بَنُو حَبيبٍ * نيُوبَهَمُ علينا يَحْرُقونَا
(At Dhū Fariqayn, on the day when the Banū Ḥabīb were grinding their teeth at us.)
Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us: Muḥammad narrated to us: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us: Ḥibbān ibn ʿAlī narrated to me from al-Kalbī from Abū Ṣāliḥ that ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib said: (لنَحرُقَنَّه) means "we will surely file it down".

farraa:102-102.t: His saying: ﴿يَوْمِئِذٍ زُرْقاً﴾: it is said: We will gather them thirsty; and it is said: We will gather them blind.

farraa:103-103.t: His saying: ﴿يَتَخَافَتُونَ بَيْنَهُمْ﴾: al-takhāfut is speech kept low.

farraa:104-104.t: His saying: ﴿أَمْثَلُهُمْ طَرِيقَةً﴾: the best of them in speech, in himself and in their view: ﴿إِن لَّبِثْتُمْ إِلاَّ يَوْماً﴾ — and he lied.

farraa:105-105.t: His saying: ﴿يَنسِفُهَا رَبِّي نَسْفاً﴾: He uproots them.

farraa:106-106.t: His saying: ﴿قَاعاً صَفْصَفاً﴾: al-qāʿ is a place where water collects, and al-ṣafṣaf is the smooth ground on which there is no vegetation.

farraa:107-107.t: His saying: ﴿وَلاۤ أَمْتاً﴾: al-amt is a hillock of ground: what rises from it; and it is said: the water-courses of the valleys (without hamza), what lies low. I have heard the Arabs say: "He filled the water-skin with a filling in which there is no amt", when there is no slackness in it. And it is said: "We travelled a journey in which there was no amt", no flagging and no weakness.

farraa:108-108.t:
His saying: ﴿يَتَّبِعُونَ ٱلدَّاعِيَ﴾: they follow the voice of the caller to the Gathering. ﴿لاعِوَجَ لَهُ﴾: He is saying: they have no deviation from the caller. It was permissible for Him to say (له) because the sense refers to the caller and his voice. It is as you say in speech: "You called me with a call from which I have no deviation for you", i.e. I do not turn aside for you or from you.
His saying: ﴿إِلاَّ هَمْساً﴾: it is said: the shuffling of feet towards the place of Gathering; and it is said: it is the faint sound. It is reported of [114 b] Ibn ʿAbbās that he quoted:
وهُنَّ يمشين بنا هميساً * إن تصدق الطير نِنك لميسا
(And they walk with us with a soft tread; if the birds' omen proves true, we shall be with Lamīs.)
This is the sound of the camels' hoofs in their travel.

farraa:109-109.t:
His saying: ﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ لاَّ تَنفَعُ ٱلشَّفَاعَةُ إِلاَّ مَنْ أَذِنَ لَهُ﴾: (من) is in the position of the accusative: intercession will not benefit anyone except one on whose behalf permission to intercede has been given.
His saying: ﴿وَرَضِيَ لَهُ قَوْلاً﴾ is like your saying "and He accepted his deed from him". A man may say: "I have accepted your deed for you" and "I have accepted it from you."

farraa:110-110.t: His saying: ﴿يَعْلَمُ مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَمَا خَلْفَهُمْ﴾ means His angels, whom those who worshipped them worshipped. So He said: they do not know what is before them and what is behind them; He is the One who knows it. That is His saying: ﴿وَلاَ يُحِيطُونَ بِهِ عِلْماً﴾.

farraa:111-111.t:
His saying: ﴿وَعَنَتِ ٱلْوُجُوهُ لِلْحَيِّ ٱلْقَيُّومِ﴾: it is said: they toiled for Him, they worked for Him. It is also related that it is the Muslim's placing his hands, his forehead and his knees [Translator's note: on the ground] when he prostrates and bows. In the sense of the Arabic language it is a man's saying ʿanawtu laka: I have submitted to you and obeyed you. It is said: "The earth did not ʿanu with anything", i.e. it did not grow anything; and it is said "lam taʿni bi-shayʾ", the meaning being the same, just as it is said ḥathawtu ʿalayhi al-turāb and ḥathaytu al-turāb ("I strewed earth on him"). Al-ʿanwa, in the Arabs' saying "I took this thing ʿanwatan", may be by force, and may be by surrender and obedience on the part of the one from whom the thing is taken. The poet said:
فما أخذوهَا عن مودَّةٍ * ولكن بضرب المشرفىّ استقَالَهَا
(They did not take it out of affection, but by the blow of the Mashrafī sword he sought its release.)
This is in the sense of obedience and surrender without fighting [Translator's note: this is how the source applies the verse; the verse itself speaks of the sword].

farraa:112-112.t: His saying: ﴿فَلاَ يَخَافُ ظُلْماً وَلاَ هَضْماً﴾: the Arabs say: "I made a haḍm for you from my right", i.e. I reduced it. It has come from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, on the Day of the Camel, that it was said to him: "Is it haḍm or retaliation?" He said: "Whatever was done is under these two feet of mine", thereby making it unavenged. It is reduction.

farraa:113-113.t:
His saying: ﴿أَوْ يُحْدِثُ لَهُمْ ذِكْراً﴾:
honour; it is like Allah's saying ﴿وَإنَّه لَذِكْرٌ لكَ ولِقَوْمِكَ﴾, i.e. an honour. And it is said: ﴿أَوْ يُحْدِثُ لَهُمْ ذِكْراً﴾ means a punishment, i.e. they will remember the descent of the punishment they were promised.

farraa:114-114.t: His saying: ﴿وَلاَ تَعْجَلْ بِٱلْقُرْآنِ مِن قَبْلِ إَن يُقْضَىٰ إِلَيْكَ وَحْيُهُ﴾: when Gabriel came to him ﷺ with the revelation, he would hasten to recite it before Gabriel had completed his recitation; so he was commanded not to hasten until Gabriel had completed his recitation. His saying ﴿فنسى﴾: he abandoned what he had been commanded.

farraa:115-115.t: His saying: ﴿وَلَمْ نَجِدْ لَهُ عَزْماً﴾: no firm resolve and no resoluteness in what he did.

farraa:117-117.t: His saying: ﴿فَلاَ يُخْرِجَنَّكُمَا مِنَ ٱلْجَنَّةِ فَتَشْقَىٰ﴾: He did not say "fa-tashqayā" (dual), because Adam is the one addressed, and his act suffices for the act of the woman. Similar to it is His saying in Qāf: ﴿عَنِ اليَميِنِ وَعَنِ الشِّمَالِ قَعِيد﴾: He made do with qaʿīd for its companion, because the meaning is known. The meaning of (فَتَشْقَىٰ) is: you will eat from the toil of your hand and your labour.

farraa:118-118.t: His saying: ﴿إِنَّ لَكَ أَلاَّ تَجُوعَ فِيهَا﴾: an there is in the position of the accusative, because when inna, layta and laʿalla are followed by an adverbial phrase (ṣifa) you put what comes after it in the accusative; and anna is of that kind.

farraa:119-119.t:
His saying: ﴿وَأَنَّكَ لاَ تَظْمَأُ فِيهَا﴾ is also accusative. Whoever reads ﴿وَإِنَّكَ لاَ تَظْمَأُ﴾ refers it back to His saying (إنَّ), which comes before (لك). It is also permissible to begin it anew and give it kasra without conjoining it to anything. Had you made ﴿وَأَنَّكَ لاَ تَظْمَأُ﴾ with fatḥa a new beginning, intending the nominative for it, in the sense of "and yours is that you will not thirst in it nor be exposed to the sun", it would have been correct.
His saying: ﴿وَلاَ تَضْحَىٰ﴾: no harmful sun will strike you. It is mentioned in some exegesis that (وَلاَ تَضْحَىٰ) means "you will not sweat", but the first is closer to being right. The poet said:
رأت رجلا أمَّا إذا الشمس أعرضت * فيَضْحَى وأمَّا بالعَشِىْ فيَخصر
(She saw a man who, when the sun shows itself broadly, is scorched by it, and in the evening is pinched with cold.)
So he has made it clear. One also says: ḍaḥītu.

farraa:121-121.t: His saying: ﴿وَطَفِقَا يَخْصِفَانِ﴾: in Arabic it is: "they set about patching" and "they began patching". Likewise His saying ﴿فطَفِق مَسْحاً بالسوق والأعناقِ﴾. (And it is said here:) they began sticking fig leaves on themselves, while it kept falling off them.

farraa:122-122.t: His saying: ﴿ثُمَّ ٱجْتَبَاهُ رَبُّهُ﴾: He chose him. ﴿فَتَابَ عَلَيْهِ وَهَدَىٰ﴾: i.e. He guided him to repentance.

farraa:124-124.t:
His saying: ﴿مَعِيشَةً ضَنكاً﴾: al-ḍank is severe narrowness.
His saying: ﴿وَنَحْشُرُهُ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيامَةِ أَعْمَىٰ﴾: blind to the proof; and it is said: he comes out of his grave seeing, then becomes blind at his Gathering.

farraa:128-128.t:
His saying: ﴿أَفَلَمْ يَهْدِ لَهُمْ﴾: does it not make clear to them, if they look, ﴿كَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا﴾? (كم) is in the position of the accusative; it cannot be otherwise. Similar to it in speech: "Has it not been made clear to you: whoever does good is rewarded for it?" — the clause of the speech has in it the sense of a nominative. Similar to it is your saying: "It has become clear to me: did ʿAbd Allāh stand or Zayd?" — in the interrogative there is the sense of a nominative. Likewise His saying: ﴿سَوَاءٌ عَلَيْكُمْ أَدَعَوْتُمْوهُمْ أَمْ أَنتُم صَامِتُون﴾: there is in it something in the nominative because of ﴿سَوَاءٌ عليكم﴾ which does not show with the interrogative; and had you said "Your silence and your calling are the same to you", the nominative within the clause would have become clear.
His saying: ﴿يَمْشُونَ فِي مَسَاكِنِهِمْ﴾ means the people of Mecca. They used to trade and travel in the dwellings of ʿĀd and Thamūd and pass through them. So the walking belongs to the unbelievers of the people of Mecca, (and the dwellings) to those destroyed. So He said: Do they not fear that there will befall them what befell those whose dwellings and the traces of whose punishment they saw?

farraa:129-129.t: His saying: ﴿وَلَوْلاَ كَلِمَةٌ سَبَقَتْ مِن رَّبِّكَ لَكَانَ لِزَاماً وَأَجَلٌ مُّسَمًّى﴾: He means: "Were it not for a word and an appointed term, it would have been inevitable" (brought forward and put back). It is — according to what they have mentioned — the killing that came down upon them at the battle of Badr.

farraa:130-131.t:
His saying: ﴿وَأَطْرَافَ ٱلنَّهَارِ﴾: the day has only two ends (ṭarafān), and the exegetes said: (and the ends of the day) are the dawn, noon and afternoon prayers. (That is) one way: that you make noon and afternoon part of the latter end of the day, then add the dawn to them, so they become "ends". It may also refer to two prayers, and that is permissible: they would be two ends treated as a plural, as He said ﴿إنْ تَتُوبا إلَى اللّهِ فَقَدْ صَغَتْ قُلُوبُكُمَا﴾. That is the dearer of the two ways to me, because He said ﴿وَأَقِمْ الصَّلاَةَ طَرفَى النَّهَارِ وَزُلَفاً مِنَ اللَّيلِ﴾. You put aṭrāf in the accusative by referring it back to "before the rising of the sun and before its setting". If you wish, you put aṭrāf in the genitive, meaning "and glorify Him in part of the night and in the ends of the day"; but I have not heard it in recitation. It is, however, like His saying ﴿وَمِنَ اللَّيْلِ فَسَبِّحْهُ وَأَدبَارَ السُّجُودِ﴾, ﴿وإدبارَ السجودِ﴾ — Ḥamza read wa-idbāra al-sujūd. In the alif, fatḥa and kasra are both permissible, but kasra of the alif is good only in recitation.
His saying ﴿لَعَلَّكَ تَرْضَىٰ﴾ and ﴿تُرْضَى﴾: their meaning is the same, because when you are pleased, you have been made pleased. Ḥamza and the companions [Translator's note: the text has «وأصحال», evidently for «وأصحاب»] of ʿAbd Allāh used to read it turḍā. Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us: Muḥammad narrated to us: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us: Abū Bakr and his brother al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAyyāsh narrated to me from ʿĀṣim from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān that he read laʿallaka (turḍā, with ḍamma on the tāʾ).
His saying: ﴿وَلاَ تَمُدَّنَّ عَيْنَيْكَ إِلَىٰ مَا مَتَّعْنَا بِهِ أَزْوَاجاً مِّنْهُمْ﴾: He means: men among them.
His saying ﴿زَهْرَةَ ٱلْحَيَاةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا﴾: you put al-zahra in the accusative by the verb: "We gave them enjoyment of it as a splendour in [115 b] the life [Translator's note: of this world] and an adornment in it." (Zahratan), even though it is definite — the Arabs say: "I passed by him, the noble, the generous" (in the accusative). One of the Banū Faqʿas recited to me:
أبعد الذى بالسَّفح سفحِ كُواكبٍ * رهينةَ رَمْسٍ من تراب وجندل
(Is it after the one at the foot of the hill, the foot of Kuwākib, held in pledge by a grave of earth and stones…?)
He put al-rahīna in the accusative by the verb, though what governs the noun which is al-rahīna is a word of the genitive [Translator's note: the text has «وفع», evidently for «وقع»]; so this is weaker than (متَّعنا) and the like.

farraa:132-132.t: His saying: ﴿لاَ نَسْأَلُكَ رِزْقاً﴾: a wage for that. Likewise His saying ﴿وَرِزقُ رَبِّك﴾: He means: and the reward of your Lord.

farraa:134-134.t: His saying: ﴿أَنَّآ أَهْلَكْنَاهُمْ بِعَذَابٍ مِّن قَبْلِهِ﴾: before the Messenger, (they would have said): "How could we be destroyed before a messenger was sent to us?" So the hāʾ refers to Muḥammad ﷺ. And it is said that the hāʾ refers to the Revelation. Both are correct.

farraa:135-135.t:
His saying: ﴿فَسَتَعْلَمُونَ مَنْ أَصْحَابُ ٱلصِّرَاطِ ٱلسَّوِيِّ وَمَنِ ٱهْتَدَىٰ﴾: both man are in the position of the nominative. Everything like it in the Qurʾān is nominative when there is something after it that makes it nominative, as in His saying ﴿فَسَتَعْلَمُونَ مَنْ هُوَ فِى ضلالٍ مُبِينٍ﴾, and similarly ﴿لنَعْلمَ أىُّ الحِزْبَيْنِ أحْصَى﴾, and similarly ﴿أعْلَمُ مَنْ جَاءَ بِالهُدَى وَمَنْ هُوَ فِى ضَلاَلٍ مُبِين﴾. Had it been put in the accusative, it would have been correct; it would be on a par with Allah's saying ﴿اللّهُ يَعْلَمُ المُفْسِدَ مِنَ المُصْلِحِ﴾.
His saying: ﴿فَسَتَعْلَمُونَ مَنْ أَصْحَابُ ٱلصِّرَاطِ ٱلسَّوِيِّ﴾: those who did not go astray; ﴿وَمَنِ ٱهْتَدَىٰ﴾: of those who were astray and then were guided.

muyesser-irab:1-1.t: ﴿طه﴾: the discussion of the disjointed letters (al-ḥurūf al-muqaṭṭaʿa) has already been given at the beginning of Sūrat al-Baqara.

muyesser-irab:2-2.t: ﴿ما أنزلنا عليك القرآن لتشقى﴾: (ما) is negating; (أنزلنا) is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); (عليك) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أنزلنا﴾; (القرآن) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿لتشقى﴾: the lām is for causation (taʿlīl), and (تشقى) is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied (muḍmara) an after the lām; the interpreted maṣdar formed from ﴿أن﴾ and the verb is genitive (majrūr) by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ﴿أنزلنا﴾.

muyesser-irab:3-3.t: ﴿إلا تذكرة لمن يخشى﴾: (إلا) is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); (تذكرة) is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose) [Translator's note: the source has the misprint «لأجه» for «لأجله»]; the exception is disconnected (munqaṭiʿ); it is also said: (تذكرة) is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial).

muyesser-irab:4-4.t:
﴿تنزيلا﴾: a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of a verb that is obligatorily omitted, its implied form being "We sent it down a sending-down" (نزلناه تنزيلًا); it is also said: a badal (substitute) from (تذكرة) if that is taken as a ḥāl (circumstantial); it is also said: accusative on account of praise and specialisation (al-madḥ wa-l-ikhtiṣāṣ); and it is also said: made accusative by ﴿يخشى﴾ as its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), i.e.: Allah sent it down as a reminder for whoever fears the sending-down of Allah.
﴿ممن﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تنزيلًا﴾.
﴿خلق الأرض﴾: a past verb, the fāʿil (agent) being latent (mustatir), and a mafʿūl bihi.
﴿والسماوات﴾: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ﴿الأرض﴾, accusative (manṣūb). The clause (خلق الأرض والسماوات) is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿من﴾, with no grammatical position.
﴿العلا﴾: a naʿt (adjective).

muyesser-irab:5-5.t: ﴿الرحمن على العرش استوى﴾: (الرحمن) is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "He" (هو), or it is a mubtadaʾ; (على العرش) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) (استوى); and the clause (استوى) is a second khabar of the implied ﴿هو﴾, or the khabar of (الرحمن).

muyesser-irab:6-6.t: ﴿له ما في السماوات وما في الأرض وما بينهما وما تحت الثرى﴾: (له) is a fronted khabar (predicate), and (ما) is a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿في السماوات﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted [word] that is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾, and the ṣila clause has no grammatical position; ﴿ما في الأرض﴾ is conjoined to (ما في السماوات); (ما بينهما) is likewise conjoined; (ما) is conjoined to (ما); and (تحت الثرى) is an adverb attached to an omitted [word] that is the ṣila of ﴿ما﴾, and the ṣila clause has no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:7-7.t: ﴿وإن تجهر بالقول فإنه يعلم السر وأخفى﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and the clause after it is resumptive, with no grammatical position; (إن) is conditional; (تجهر) is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "you" (أنت); (بالقول) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تجهر﴾; (فإنه): the fāʾ is connective (rābiṭa) because the apodosis (jawāb) is a nominal clause; (إن) is an abrogating (nāsikh) particle, and the hāʾ is a pronoun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the accusative as the noun of inna; the clause (يعلم السر) is the khabar (predicate) of inna; and (أخفى) is an elative noun (ism tafḍīl) conjoined to (السر), i.e.: "more hidden than it"; it is also said: it is a past verb, i.e.: and Allah has hidden His unseen from His servants.

muyesser-irab:8-8.t:
﴿الله﴾: a mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿لا﴾: the lā of generic negation.
﴿إله﴾: its noun (ism), indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa in the position of the accusative.
﴿إلا﴾: a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr).
﴿هو﴾: a badal (substitute) from the position of (لا) and its noun, because their position is nominative as a mubtadaʾ; or a badal from the pronoun latent in the omitted khabar (predicate). The clause ﴿لا إله إلا هو﴾ is the khabar.
﴿له الأسماء الحسنى﴾: ﴿له﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted [word] that is a fronted khabar; (الأسماء) is a postponed mubtadaʾ; (الحسنى) is a naʿt (adjective) of (الأسماء); and the clause is a second khabar.

muyesser-irab:9-9.t: ﴿وهل أتاك حديث موسى﴾: the wāw is for resumption, and the clause after it is resumptive, with no grammatical position; (أتاك) is a verb and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (حديث موسى) is the fāʿil (agent); and the interrogation is for affirmation (taqrīr).

muyesser-irab:10-10.t:
﴿إذ رأى نارا فقال لأهله امكثوا إني آنست نارا﴾: ﴿إذ﴾ is an adverb of past time attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿حديث﴾ in the preceding ayah; the clause ﴿رأى﴾ is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (نارًا) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (فقال) is conjoined to (رأى); (لأهله) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (قال); the clause (امكثوا) is the content of the speech (maqūl al-qawl); the clause (إني) gives the reason for the command to stay; (إن) is an abrogating (nāsikh) particle, and the yāʾ is a pronoun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the accusative as the noun of inna; the clause (آنست) is the khabar (predicate) of inna; and (نارًا) is a mafʿūl bihi.
